Observed at +14.855287790298462s — page 9
th it — a case can pass with a failing trial in it,\n so tallying diagnostics gives a different answer than the platform reached.
\n* **`verdict: \"notEstablished\"` is not a failure and not `inconclusive`.** It\n means no verdict exists at all (unfinished, s
topped early, or undecidable);\n `undecided.reason` says which. `inconclusive` *is* a decision — the validity\n phase ran and wi
thheld a verdict.\n* **`diagnostics.complete` says whether you have the whole list.** A page\n fetched with a `cursor` is never c

omplete, and `scannedIterations` separates
 "nothing failed" from "we did not look".

Evidence is scoped to the claim it s
upports: for a measured failure the span\nids, prompt indexes and reasons come from the first failed stage's row alone,\nand `evid

ence.tracePath` is an API-relative path you can append to your base URL
to read the full trace.

`model` takes an id from the h
osted catalog — `provider/name` form, e.g.\n`anthropic/claude-haiku-4.5` — and runs on your organization's credits.\nProvider-nati
ve ids (e.g. `claude-sonnet-4-5`) are bring-your-own-key: pass\nthe key in `modelApiKeys`. A model the API can't execute is reject

ed at
create time with `VALIDATION_ERROR`; `details.hostedModels` lists the valid
hosted ids for that provider.

Reruns are ev
en shorter: `{ \"suiteId\": \"...\" }` reruns the suite exactly as\nconfigured, connecting the suite's saved server selection (the
`202` response\nlists the resolved `servers`). Pass `serverIds` to override the selection; a\nsuite with no saved selection requi

res it (`VALIDATION_ERROR` with
`details.reason: "NO_SAVED_SERVER_SELECTION"` otherwise).

### Running against a project envi

ronment

A [project environment](#endpoints) is launchable only through a suite that has
it **attached**. Attach them first wit
h\n`PATCH /projects/{projectId}/eval-suites/{suiteId}` and an `environmentIds`\narray (send `null` to detach them all; `[]` is rej
ected — use `null`), then\npass `environmentId` on the run. It must be one of that suite's attached\nenvironments; anything else i

s a `400` with
`details.reason: "ENVIRONMENT_NOT_ATTACHED"`, raised before any case is
authored or any server connected.

Om
itting `environmentId` is meaningful, and depends on the suite:\n\n* **no** attached environments → the run uses the saved server
selection, as before;\n* **exactly one** attached → that environment is used automatically. The `202`\n response's `environment`

field says so;
* **several** attached → `400` with `details.reason: "ENVIRONMENT_REQUIRED"`,
 naming the candidates.

The e
nvironment supplies the closed server set — including the servers its\npinned plugin versions contribute — so `serverIds` is not r
equired and is\n**rejected** alongside it (`400`), rather than accepted and ignored: honoring\nboth would connect a different set
than the run is stamped with. The same goes\nfor a `serverIds` override on an environment-based suite\n(`details.reason: \"ENVIRON

MENT_SERVERS_NOT_OVERRIDABLE"`).

The run is pinned to the environment revision resolved at launch: if the
environment changes
in between, the run is rejected with `CONFLICT` (409)\nrather than executing against a different configuration than the one whose

tools were captured. Use
`GET /projects/{projectId}/environments/{environmentId}/resolve` to see what it
will connect before l
aunching.\n\nWhen creating a new inline suite, `POST .../eval-runs` also accepts `hosts: [{ host: \"Claude\", servers: [\"my-serve
r\"] }]`, using the same host name or ID and optional server selection as `POST .../eval-suites`. A single host is selected for th
e run automatically. With multiple attachments, use `namedHostId` to select the run's client. For an existing suite, update its at
tachments first. If `hosts` is omitted, the backend supplies the project's default client.\n\nRun reads and listings expose `clien
t: { id, name, source, hostStyle?, modelId? }` when recorded. `id` is the named host ID or `null`; `source` is `environment`, `att
ached_host`, `suite_default`, or `sdk`. The name is durable even if the host is deleted. SDK executions use `SDK harness`; `launch
er.client` separately identifies the launching process. Older runs without a descriptor omit `client`. `modelSource: \"case\"` mea
ns the run's sole model came from its case snapshot; `client_default` and `override` retain their existing meanings.\n\nEvery run
records which environment it used. `GET .../eval-runs/{runId}` (and\nthe run listings) return `environment: { id, name, revision }
` — read from the\nrun's immutable snapshot, not the suite's current attachments — or `null` for a\nrun that used a saved server s

election.

Per-organization
concurrency is capped (default **2** concurrent runs); exceeding it returns
`429` with `details.re

ason: "CONCURRENT_RUN_LIMIT"` — wait for an active run
to finish.

If a server answers `401 OAUTH_REQUIRED`, complete the OAu
th flow yourself\n(the SDK's `runOAuthLogin` handles interactive, headless, and\nclient-credentials flows) and upload the token to
one of the server's\n[accounts](#server-accounts). Subsequent runs inject the stored token, and\nrefresh it server-side when you

stored a refresh token.

## Reasoning effort

A reasoning effort is a **saved setting on a model selection**, not a free-stand
ing\nfield. A `ModelSelection` (`modelId`, `source`, an optional `connectionRef`, and a\n`fallback`) carries it as `settings.reaso

ningEffort`, and the same shape is
accepted everywhere a model choice is saved:

| Where | Field |
| - | - |
| Client (`PATCH
/projects/{projectId}/clients/{client}`) | `set.modelSelection` (or `config.modelSelection` on a whole-config replacement) |\n| P
roject environment (`POST`, `PATCH`, `POST .../ensure-adhoc`) | `modelSelection`, read back on the environment |\n| Eval case (`PO
ST`, `PATCH .../cases`) | `models[].selection`, read back on the case |\n| Eval suite (`PATCH /projects/{projectId}/eval-suites/{s

lId": "openai/gpt-5",
 "source": "hosted",
 "settings": { "reasoningEffort": "high" },
 "fallback": { "provi
of\n them a model accepts is `supportedReasoningEfforts` on each row of the public\n `GET /v1/models` catalog. An empty or absen
t list means no effort is offered for\n that model — do not guess one.\n* **Applied or refused, never dropped.** A saved effort i
s applied by the route\n the run takes and recorded on the execution record, or refused with\n `capability_missing` before any s
pend. An effort replaces the sampling\n temperature.\n* **A selection belongs to one model.** It must be for the `model` / `model
Id` it\n sits beside (`400` otherwise); sent alone it pins its own model. A bare model\n change on a suite or environment drops
a selection saved for the old model\n instead of failing.\n* **Cases keep their selections.** A `models` PATCH replaces the array
, but an\n entry that omits `selection` keeps the case's existing selection for that\n model. Send `selection: null` to drop it.

* **Clearing.** `null` clears a saved selection on a client `set`, an environment
 or a suite, keeping the bare model id.
* *
*Never a secret.** A selection has no credential field; an unknown key\n (`apiKey`, …) is a `400`.\n* **Environments need the cap
ability.** `GET .../environments/capabilities`\n reports `modelSelections`; an older deployment rejects the field.\n* **`advanced
Config.reasoningEffort` is retired.** It was never applied, so\n writing it is a `400` pointing at `models[].selection.settings`,

and a stored
 value is refused by the runner.

`POST /chat-sessions/messages` takes a top-level `reasoningEffort` for a
per-
request effort. Like `temperature`, it is pinned on the session's **first\nturn** (a continuation that restates it is refused), it

wins over the effort a
`hostId`'s saved selection carries, and it cannot be combined with `temperature`.

The SDK, CLI, MCP to
ols and in-app agent all go through the same operations:\n`--effort` / `reasoningEffort` is a shorthand that edits the selection t

he target
already has, and is refused (`send modelSelection`) when there is none.
